description: FLUXA scenario library. Onsets are hours from simulation start. A is the unperturbed reference; B-F are the required disturbance set with F as the primary compound resilience experiment; G and H are supplementary network/integration experiments. Scenarios whose required safety level is SENSITIVE (D, F) are gated by QRADLE invariant 1 and will not execute without human authorization.

scenarios.name: Baseline
scenarios.description: Normal generation and demand. No perturbation. Reference trajectory for all comparisons.

scenarios.name: Solar shock
scenarios.description: Photovoltaic output falls 70% over 15 minutes at 12:00, holds for 2 hours, then recovers over 45 minutes.

scenarios.name: Wind shock
scenarios.description: Wind generation falls 85% over 20 minutes at 18:00 (into the evening peak), holds 3 hours, recovers over 60 minutes.

scenarios.name: Generator outage
scenarios.description: The CCGT trips instantaneously at 19:00 and stays out for 3 hours. SENSITIVE: requires human authorization under QRADLE invariant 1.

scenarios.name: Load spike
scenarios.description: Demand rises 30% over 30 minutes at 17:30, holds 2 hours, decays over 60 minutes.

scenarios.name: Compound event
scenarios.description: Primary resilience experiment: wind collapse at 18:00, CCGT trip at 18:50, and a 25% demand surge at 19:00, overlapping through the evening peak. SENSITIVE: requires human authorization.

scenarios.name: Transmission derate
scenarios.description: Supplementary network experiment. The B3-B5 corridor (L5) carries the wind farm's output to the urban load centre and is the most heavily loaded branch in the baseline (0.836 utilisation at 08:00). It is derated 55% for 4 hours from 06:00, across the morning demand ramp. The energy balance is not short, so this isolates the network constraint: the expected response is congestion-driven wind curtailment with the limit binding but not violated.

scenarios.name: Solar congestion with low demand
scenarios.description: Supplementary renewable-integration experiment. Both corridors out of the photovoltaic bus B2 (L1 to B1, L3 to B4) are derated 70% for 4 hours from 10:00 while midday demand falls 40%, so the solar resource exceeds what the network and the remaining sinks (export, storage, the CCGT's must-run floor) can absorb. On this capacity mix a pure demand reduction produces almost no curtailment -- export and storage absorb the surplus -- so congestion is what makes the curtailment pathway observable.
